Autumn Colour Routes: Riding Through Gold

Britain's autumn transformation is one of nature's great spectacles. From mid-September to early November, the landscape blazes with colour — red maples, golden birches, copper beeches, and rust-orange bracken. For motorcyclists, these colours create the most photogenic riding of the year.

Peak Colour Timing

  • Scottish Highlands: Late September to mid-October. Birch woodlands and bracken turn first.
  • Northern England: Early to mid-October. The Lake District, Dales, and Northumberland peak.
  • Central England and Wales: Mid to late October. The Wye Valley and Snowdonia are spectacular.
  • Southern England: Late October to early November. The New Forest and South Downs peak latest.

Best Autumn Colour Routes

  • Perthshire Big Tree Country: Scotland's autumn showpiece. The roads through Glen Lyon, Fortingall, and around Loch Tummel pass some of the oldest and most colourful trees in Britain. The Enchanted Forest light show at Pitlochry adds a magical evening dimension.
  • Wye Valley: The gorge section between Monmouth and Chepstow is dramatic in autumn. The beech and oak woodland blazes with colour and the road beneath forms a golden tunnel.
  • New Forest: The ancient beeches and oaks of the New Forest produce exceptional autumn colour. The B-roads winding through old woodland are magical in October.
  • Lake District: The shore of Derwentwater and the road through Borrowdale are framed by deciduous woodland that turns gold and amber. Tarn Hows is a classic autumn colour spot.
  • Forest of Dean: On the Welsh border, this ancient forest is a blaze of colour in October. The roads through the forest are atmospheric.

Photography Tips

  • Overcast days create even light that brings out colour saturation
  • Low sun through autumn leaves creates spectacular backlit effects
  • Include reflections in still water for double the colour impact
  • Your motorcycle against a backdrop of golden trees makes for stunning touring photos
Don't rush autumn colour rides. Stop frequently, walk into the woodland, and immerse yourself. The colours change daily and each visit reveals new detail. An autumn tour through Perthshire or the Wye Valley is one of Britain's great natural experiences.

Practical Considerations

  • Wet leaves on roads are treacherous — ride cautiously on tree-lined routes
  • Low sun causes dangerous glare in early morning and late afternoon
  • Shorter days mean earlier starts and earlier finishes to touring days
  • Carry warm layers — autumn temperatures drop quickly after sunset

Traffic Avoidance Tactics

Bank holiday traffic follows predictable patterns. Friday evening sees a mass exodus from cities, Saturday morning is busy on tourist routes, and Monday afternoon sees the return flow. Smart timing exploits the gaps between these peaks.

The best bank holiday riding hours are Saturday before 9am, Sunday all day (surprisingly quiet as families do non-driving activities), and Monday morning before the return traffic builds. Use these windows for your best roads and save urban or less-scenic sections for the busy periods.

Alternatively, embrace the opposite approach: tour in the opposite direction to the holiday flow. When everyone heads south to the coast, ride north to the emptier hills. Counter-flow touring on bank holidays can deliver remarkably quiet roads.

Essential Bank Holiday Planning

Book accommodation at least four weeks before any bank holiday weekend. Popular areas sell out completely, and last-minute options are limited to expensive hotels or unsuitable locations. If you're flexible about your destination, book two or three potential accommodations and cancel the ones you don't use within the cancellation window.

Pack your bike the evening before departure. A Friday evening start gets you ahead of Saturday traffic, and every minute saved in the morning is a minute extra on the road. Have your route loaded on your GPS, your tank full, and your gear ready. A bank holiday weekend is precious riding time — don't waste it on logistics.

Consider an itinerary that goes against the crowd flow. On a May bank holiday, while everyone heads south to the coast, ride north to the quiet hills. On August bank holiday, while Cornwall and the Lake District are packed, the Scottish Borders and North Pennines are gloriously empty. The Scottish Highlands peak late September to mid-October; southern England peaks late October to early November.
Perthshire Big Tree Country, the Wye Valley, the New Forest and the Lake District are the standout routes.
Wet leaves and low-sun glare are the main autumn hazards on tree-lined roads.

faq.q: When do autumn colours peak across the UK?
faq.a: Colour moves south as the season progresses. The Scottish Highlands peak late September to mid-October as birch woodlands and bracken turn first. Northern England, including the Lakes, Dales and Northumberland, peaks early to mid-October. Central England and Wales, notably the Wye Valley and Snowdonia, peak mid to late October, and southern England, such as the New Forest and South Downs, peaks latest.

faq.q: What are the best autumn-colour motorcycle routes?
faq.a: Perthshire Big Tree Country is Scotland's showpiece, with roads through Glen Lyon, Fortingall and around Loch Tummel. The Wye Valley gorge between Monmouth and Chepstow forms a golden tunnel of beech and oak. The New Forest's ancient beeches and oaks produce exceptional colour, the Lake District's Borrowdale and Derwentwater blaze gold and amber, and the Forest of Dean is a border blaze of colour.

faq.q: What are the main hazards of autumn riding?
faq.a: Wet leaves on roads are treacherous, so ride cautiously on tree-lined routes. The low autumn sun causes dangerous glare in early morning and late afternoon, so carry both a tinted and a clear visor. Shorter days mean earlier starts and finishes to touring days, and autumn temperatures drop quickly after sunset, so carry warm layers for the ride home.

faq.q: How do I photograph autumn colours from the bike?
faq.a: Overcast days create even light that brings out colour saturation, while low sun through autumn leaves produces spectacular backlit effects. Include reflections in still water for double the colour impact, and position your motorcycle against a backdrop of golden trees for stunning touring photos. Do not rush: stop frequently, walk into the woodland and immerse yourself, as the colours change daily.

faq.q: Which single route is best for a long autumn weekend?
faq.a: A long weekend in Perthshire during peak colour is outstanding, with roads through Glen Lyon, around Loch Tummel and through the forests near Pitlochry, plus the Enchanted Forest light show for an evening attraction. In England, the Wye Valley and Forest of Dean combine colour with atmospheric gorge and forest riding, and the A466 through the lower Wye Valley is among Britain's most beautiful rides in mid-October.
